title: Ethiopian Lamb Soup
community: Ethiopian celebrations — lamb bone broth for the most important occasions
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Lamb Soup — lamb bones and meat simmered slowly with Ethiopian aromatic spices into a light, deeply flavourful broth. The celebration soup — served at weddings and religious feasts as the opener, before the main wats appear.
longDesc: Lamb shorba is the Ethiopian celebration soup — lighter and more fragrant than beef shorba, it is served as the opening of a lamb celebration feast. The lamb bones produce a cleaner, more delicately flavoured broth than beef.
ingredients: 1 kg lamb bones and meat — ribs and shoulder
steps: See ETH034 — substitute lamb bones for beef.
Lamb fat is lighter than beef fat — the broth will be less rich.
chefTips: Cardamom is the distinction for lamb shorba — it pairs beautifully with lamb.
Lamb broth is lighter in colour than beef — a paler golden.
cookingScience: Lamb fat has a higher proportion of shorter-chain fatty acids than beef — these are more flavourful and more aromatic when dissolved into the broth, producing the characteristic fragrance of lamb shorba.
sustainabilityTips: Whole-animal use — bones and secondary cuts.
culturalNote: Lamb shorba at an Ethiopian celebration is the announcement that something wonderful is coming — the light, fragrant soup that opens the appetite before the great wats arrive.
